analysis:
The supplied units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 747-1220, historical release notes). The PR modifies only documentation: it replaces the v0.10.1 candidate header with a v0.10.2 candidate block (head lines 11-246, base lines 11-13). The base excerpts contain no executable code, so they give no visible line on which to cite a regression. The patch excerpt is truncated; its visible text is the v0.10.2 upgrade and rollout notes.

Relevant statements in those notes:
- Logprobs on Nemotron 3.5 Super and GLM-5.3-Flash are gated on catalog rows and on platform PR #464.
- The cache-routing allowlist tuple is a precondition for prefix caching.
- 4-bit balanced SSD checkpoints for Super and GLM-5.3-Flash become the default, under new cache namespaces.

Cache and security relevance:
- The 4-bit checkpoints touch T-041, the encrypted SSD prefix cache. The visible text says the old exact files miss once and then age out through the normal TTL sweep. It also says authenticated, scoped cache routing remains allowlist-gated, so the coordinator sends no cache scope until a model's tuple is allowlisted.
- The visible text does not change the TTL, HMAC lookup tags, salt scoping or encryption. The 30-minute TTL and the KEK-wipe purge are unchanged in the visible portion.
- The notes do reveal a behavioral difference: output from a 4-bit checkpoint is not bit-identical to cold output. This is an integrity and quality consideration, not a confidentiality regression, and it is documented honestly.

Remaining uncertainty:
- The actual code changes (KVCacheSSD, checkpoint encoding, namespace and epoch separation, and old-file TTL cleanup) are not in the supplied units. I did not verify that the new cache namespaces keep HMAC-keyed names, that AAD binds the new layout and precision profile, or that logprob gating is enforced provider-side.
- The remainder of the patch text beyond line ~25 of the new block was truncated and not examined.

No findings from these units; deeper review is advisable for the source files that implement the 4-bit checkpoint and logprob changes.
